questions.question_text: The water level in a canal lock reaches a maximum of $18.6$ m and a minimum of $5.4$ m. What are the amplitude and the mean position of a sinusoidal model of the level?

options.why: Used the full range $18.6-5.4$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Added the maximum and minimum for the mean position but forgot to divide by $2$.
Forgot to halve both the difference and the sum, so both values are doubled.

questions.solution_text:
$k=\dfrac{18.6-5.4}{2}$
$=\dfrac{13.2}{2}$
$=6.6$
$c=\dfrac{18.6+5.4}{2}$
$=\dfrac{24}{2}$
$=12$
The amplitude is $6.6$ m and the mean position is $12$ m.

questions.question_text: Successive low tides at a beach are $14$ hours apart. The depth is modelled by $y=k\cos(at)+c$, where $t$ is in hours. What is the value of $a$?

options.why: Used $a=\dfrac{T}{2\pi}$ instead of $a=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}$.
Treated $14$ hours as half a period, so used $T=28$.
Both inverted the formula and treated $14$ hours as half a period.

questions.solution_text:
Successive low tides are one full period apart.
$T=14$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}$
$=\dfrac{2\pi}{14}$
$=\dfrac{\pi}{7}$

questions.question_text: The height of a bicycle pedal above the ground is greatest at $32$ cm and least at $8$ cm, and the pedal completes one revolution every $2$ seconds. The pedal is at its highest point when $t=0$ seconds. Which model gives the height $h$ centimetres?

options.why: Chose the negative coefficient, which puts the minimum rather than the maximum at $t=0$.
Used the full range $32-8$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the full range as the amplitude and also chose the sign that puts the minimum at $t=0$.

questions.solution_text:
$k=\dfrac{32-8}{2}$
$=12$
$c=\dfrac{32+8}{2}$
$=20$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{2}$
$=\pi$
The pedal is at its maximum when $t=0$, so the coefficient of $\cos$ is positive.
$h=12\cos(\pi t)+20$

questions.question_text: A carousel horse rises and falls between $0.8$ m and $1.6$ m above the platform, completing a cycle every $6$ seconds. The horse is at its lowest point when $t=0$ seconds. Which model gives the height $h$ metres?

options.why: Used a positive coefficient, which puts the maximum rather than the minimum at $t=0$.
Used the full range $1.6-0.8$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the full range as the amplitude and the sign that puts the maximum at $t=0$.

questions.solution_text:
$k=\dfrac{1.6-0.8}{2}$
$=0.4$
$c=\dfrac{1.6+0.8}{2}$
$=1.2$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{6}$
$=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$
The horse is at its minimum when $t=0$, so the coefficient of $\cos$ is negative.
$h=-0.4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{3}\right)+1.2$

questions.question_text: An alternating current swings between $-15$ A and $15$ A and completes $60$ cycles each second. The current is $0$ and rising when $t=0$ seconds. Which model gives the current $I$ amps?

options.why: Used the full range $15-(-15)$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Used the frequency $60$ as the period, giving $a=\dfrac{2\pi}{60}$.
Used the full range as the amplitude and the frequency as the period.

questions.solution_text:
$k=\dfrac{15-(-15)}{2}$
$=15$
$c=\dfrac{15+(-15)}{2}$
$=0$
$T=\dfrac{1}{60}$
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{\frac{1}{60}}$
$=120\pi$
The current starts at the mean position and is rising, so use $\sin$ with a positive coefficient.
$I=15\sin(120\pi t)$

options.why: Used the full range $1400-600$ as the amplitude instead of half of it.
Read $18$ months as half a period, giving $a=\dfrac{2\pi}{36}$.
Used the full range as the amplitude and read $18$ months as half a period.

questions.solution_text:
From the graph the maximum is $1400$ and the minimum is $600$.
$k=\dfrac{1400-600}{2}$
$=400$
$c=\dfrac{1400+600}{2}$
$=1000$
The graph repeats every $18$ months.
$a=\dfrac{2\pi}{18}$
$=\dfrac{\pi}{9}$
The graph starts at its maximum, so the coefficient of $\cos$ is positive.
$P=400\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{9}\right)+1000$

questions.question_text: A tide reaches a maximum depth of $7.0$ m and a minimum depth of $1.4$ m. A student writes the model $y=5.6\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right)+4.2$. What is wrong with the student's model?

options.text: The amplitude should be $2.8$, because the amplitude is half the range.
The mean position should be $8.4$, because the mean position is the sum of the maximum and minimum.
options.why: Added the maximum and minimum without halving; the mean position $4.2$ is already correct.

options.text: The amplitude should be $8.4$, because the amplitude is the sum of the maximum and minimum.
options.why: Confused the amplitude with the total of the two extremes rather than half their difference.

options.text: Nothing is wrong, because $5.6$ is the difference between the maximum and the minimum.
options.why: Accepted the full range as the amplitude, which is the most common error in building these models.

questions.solution_text:
$7.0-1.4=5.6$
This is the range, not the amplitude.
$k=\dfrac{7.0-1.4}{2}$
$=2.8$
$c=\dfrac{7.0+1.4}{2}$
$=4.2$
The mean position is correct, but the amplitude should be $2.8$, half of the range.

questions.question_text: A model of the form $y=k\cos(at)+c$ is fitted to the daily maximum and minimum depths recorded at a wharf on one day. Which statement best describes a limitation of this model?

options.text: It repeats exactly forever, so it cannot show tidal ranges that grow and shrink through the month.
It cannot give a depth at $t=0$, because $\cos 0$ is undefined.
options.why: $\cos 0=1$ is perfectly defined, so the model does give a depth at $t=0$.

options.text: It can only be used for whole numbers of hours, because $t$ must be an integer.
options.why: Confuses a continuous model with a discrete one; $t$ may take any value in the domain.

options.text: It predicts that the depth eventually falls to zero, because a cosine curve decays.
options.why: Confuses a sinusoidal model with an exponential decay model; a cosine curve does not decay.

questions.solution_text:
A cosine model has a fixed amplitude, so every cycle it predicts is identical to the one before.
Real tidal ranges change from day to day through the lunar month, and weather changes them further.
So the model repeats exactly forever and cannot capture a tidal range that grows and shrinks.
